For completeness, the repair that WAS landed is confirmed exact: .executesVerbatim == naming-v6 .gates[15].executes, compared as UTF-8 bytes, True, including the U+00D7 MULTIPLICATION SIGN.
mustFix.whyThisIsNotCosmetic: The subject's stated purpose is 'Restore gate-harness-naming.v6 .gates[15].executes byte-exactly in executesVerbatim' and its .findingDisposition records CLAUDE-G16-V3-MF1 with disposition 'ACCEPTED' and landedAt ['executesVerbatim']. That disposition is an assertion to the recorder that the MUST-FIX is discharged. It is not: the file still rewrites naming-v6's executes, from the same parent, dropping the same sentence, substituting the same kind of speaker sentence. A recorder who trusts the ACCEPTED disposition and reads .basedOn.namingV6.role will carry 'This v4 remasures occupancy of that unversioned identifier' forward as naming-v6 executes content, because the sentence immediately preceding it genuinely is naming-v6 executes content and the source's own terminating sentence has been removed. The subject's declared discipline is 'SPECIFICATION OF EXACT-BYTE INTENT' and its authority rests on quotation fidelity to pinned sources; a partial repair that is declared complete is worse for the register than an unrepaired file, because it retires the finding.
mustFix.repair: In .basedOn.namingV6.role, restore the full naming-v6 .gates[15].executes value and its terminating field label exactly as frozen v1 and frozen v2 carry it: '... namingStanding NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED. executes: Change-impact corpus × component/language/platform matrix. Owner cell was made concrete 2026-08-13 (C4). This candidate does not change that owner. doesNotClaim QUALIFIED. This v4 remasures occupancy of that unversioned identifier. naming v6 and G16 harness occupancy are different lineages; their version numbers are unrelated. Not this artifact's version number.' That is the G07 v4 / G08 v3 / G16 v1 / G16 v2 shape and requires no new bytes - every restored byte already exists in the pinned parent. Then update .findingDisposition for CLAUDE-G16-V3-MF1 to landedAt ['executesVerbatim', 'basedOn.namingV6.role'], and extend .failsIf[0] so the fail condition covers every site that reproduces naming-v6 executes, not only .executesVerbatim.
mustFix.severityRationale: Graded MUST-FIX on the same rule the v3 cycle applied: the defect is not interpretive. The bytes of a colon-introduced reproduction of a digest-pinned, dual-ACCEPT parent field provably differ from that parent, the convention that the reproduction is byte-complete is established by four independent artifacts including this lineage's own frozen v1 and ACCEPT-0/0 v2, and it is a regression those predecessors did not have. It is additionally graded MUST-FIX rather than SHOULD-FIX because the subject affirmatively records the governing MUST-FIX as ACCEPTED while the defect it names survives in the file; an incorrect discharge claim is a standing defect, not a wording defect. A coordinator who prefers to reserve MUST-FIX strictly for live-state defects may regrade it SHOULD-FIX; the decision rule for this cycle is unchanged either way, since ACCEPT requires 0 SHOULD-FIX and this review also carries CLAUDE-G16-V4-SF1.

Frozen v1 stays unmoved.' .failsIf still carries only 'v2 is recorded as a current occupancy remasurement'. registerRowNote is the register-facing note a recorder reads when pinning DR-G16; its closing roster is what tells that recorder which predecessor artifacts must stay unmoved at 0444. As it stands the roster enumerates predecessors as though v2 were the immediate one, and the freshly frozen 0444 Claude-REJECT v3 - the artifact whose immobility this entire cycle depends on, since v4's authority is that v3's two findings landed against an unmoved v3 - is absent from both rosters.
measurement: Live modes confirmed: v1, v2, v3 and v4 are all -r--r--r-- (0444). v3 is frozen and unmoved; its digest 30e08b3b01f082664f7d2471508742f67e41a0b3cc937de6b1beb3a278c472ee recomputes to the value the subject pins.

Leaf diff v3 -> v4: 94 leaves changed. .registerRowNote is NOT among them - it is carried byte-identically from v3. .failsIf[12] 'v2 is recorded as a current occupancy remasurement' is likewise carried unchanged (it sits at index 10 in v3 and index 12 in v4 only because two entries were prepended).

Convention, measured across every occupancy artifact in the corpus that carries a frozen roster in registerRowNote: G10 v2 -> [v1]; G14 v2 -> [v1]; G14 v3 -> [v2, v1]; G14 v4 -> [v3, v2, v1]; G15 v8 -> [v7]; G15 v9 -> [v8, v7]; G16 v3 -> [v2, v1]. In all seven the roster is headed by v(N-1). G15 shows the roster may be truncated to the two most recent (v9 lists v8 and v7, not v8..v1), so completeness back to v1 is not the invariant - leading with the immediate predecessor is.

G16 v4 -> [v2, v1] is the only artifact in the corpus that carries a roster and does not head it with v(N-1). Under G14's full-roster shape it should read [v3, v2, v1]; under G15's truncated shape [v3, v2]. Either way v3 must lead.

The closest structural twin makes the correct handling explicit: harness.DR-G14.language-runtime-ux.typescript.v4 (D-213 ADOPTED, dual 0/0, same date, v4 of its lineage) closes registerRowNote 'Frozen v3 stays unmoved. Frozen v2 stays unmoved. Frozen v1 stays unmoved.'
